	<h2>Description</h2>

<p>The BCM Recce-11 is built around a compact, close-quarters role where a full-length rifle would be a liability. It suits shooters who need a rifle that handles tight spaces without sacrificing the reliability and build quality associated with Bravo Company’s professional-grade line. The platform is a direct-impingement AR-15, and at this barrel length the gas system is tuned to extract reliably from a shorter dwell time — a balance BCM works out carefully because shorter barrels can drive bolt carrier velocity up, increasing felt recoil and wear if the system is not correctly spec’d for the configuration.</p>
<p>Chambered for .223 Rem and 5.56 NATO, the rifle accepts both cartridge types, which gives the shooter flexibility in ammunition selection without running a dedicated single-caliber build. The 30-round magazine capacity covers standard AR magazine format, and the semi-automatic action keeps the manual of arms straightforward for anyone already familiar with the AR platform.</p>
<p>BCM’s Recce-series rifles are intended to be complete, working configurations rather than starting points for a parts build. That matters because gas tuning, barrel, and upper receiver geometry are treated as a matched system at the factory rather than assembled from separate-sourced components. The result is a rifle that is meant to run as-delivered without requiring the shooter to troubleshoot component compatibility before the first range session.</p>
<p>At 11 inches, velocity will be lower than a carbine-length barrel produces, which is worth factoring into ammunition selection if terminal performance at distance is a consideration. Within typical close- to mid-range distances, the trade-off in velocity is offset by the significant gain in maneuverability the shorter profile provides.</p>
